dialect.detail: Italian ERP/warehouse management system, likely compiled with GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) on Linux/Unix. Uses .sl file extensions for SELECT copybooks and .fd for FD copybooks, COMP-1 for numeric, 78-level constants, and Italian-language identifiers/comments. Possibly Passepartout or similar Italian SME ERP.
evidence: Italian comments and variable names (giacenza, impegnato, ordini, magazzino)
DECLARATIVES with USE AFTER ERROR sections

purpose.domain_detail: Warehouse/inventory management: recalculates dynamic stock values (giacenza=stock, impegnato=committed, ordinato=ordered) from credit notes, unfulfilled orders, warehouse movements, supplier orders, and master orders. Runs nightly as a batch job after zeroing dynamic values on progmag (stock progress file).
purpose.summary: Nightly batch program that recalculates dynamic inventory values (stock on hand, committed quantities, ordered quantities) from various transaction sources including credit notes, unfulfilled orders, warehouse movements, and supplier/master orders. It processes multiple indexed files and updates a stock progress file (progmag), with full error handling and email notification support.

notable_features: 72 COPY statements for modular file definitions (.sl/.fd pattern)
USE AFTER ERROR DECLARATIVES for each file
ALTERNATE RECORD KEY with multiple fields
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 2054 lines. No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS. The .sl/.fd copybook naming convention and Italian business domain strongly suggest an Italian SME ERP system, possibly GnuCOBOL-based. COMP-3 count is 0 which is unusual for financial data but may be in copybooks. The program has extensive error handling and is clearly production code.
